questions.question: A metallic solid cuboid of dimensions 36 cm × 18 cm × 12 cm is melted and recast in the form of cubes of side 6 cm. Find the number of cubes so formed.
questions.questionHtml: A metallic solid cuboid of dimensions 36 cm × 18 cm × 12 cm is melted and recast in the form of cubes of side 6 cm. Find the number of cubes so formed.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a solid is melted and recast into smaller solids, the total volume remains constant.

Number of cubes = Total Volume of Cuboid ÷ Volume of 1 Cube

n = (36 × 18 × 12) ÷ (6 × 6 × 6)

n = (36 ÷ 6) × (18 ÷ 6) × (12 ÷ 6)

n = 6 × 3 × 2 = 36

∴ The correct answer is 36.

Alternate Method

Given:

Dimensions of the metallic solid cuboid = 36 cm × 18 cm × 12 cm

Side of the newly formed cubes = 6 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of a cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

Volume of a cube = Side3

Number of cubes formed = Volume of Cuboid ÷ Volume of 1 Cube

Calculation:

⇒ Volume of the given cuboid = 36 × 18 × 12 cm3

⇒ Volume of one small cube = 6 × 6 × 6 cm3

⇒ Number of cubes = (36 × 18 × 12) ÷ (6 × 6 × 6)

⇒ Number of cubes = (36 ÷ 6) × (18 ÷ 6) × (12 ÷ 6)

⇒ Number of cubes = 6 × 3 × 2

⇒ Number of cubes = 36

∴ The correct answer is 36.

Additional Information

Melting and Recasting Principle

When a 3D solid object is melted and recast into another shape, the volume of material remains conserved. (Total Volume1 = Total Volume2).

Surface Area

Total Surface Area of a Cube = 6a2. Total Surface Area of a Cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl). Surface area changes upon recasting, but volume remains constant.

Longest Diagonal

The length of the longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is given by √(l2 + b2 + h2). For a cube of side a, the diagonal is a√3.

questions.question: If the volume of a cube is 1728 m 3 , then find the perimeter of one face of the cube.
questions.questionHtml: If the volume of a cube is 1728 m<sup>3</sup>, then find the perimeter of one face of the cube.
questions.solution:
Side of cube = \(\sqrt[3]{volume} = \sqrt[3]{1728}=12\:m\)

Perimeter of one face =  4a = 4 x 12 = 48 m

questions.question: If the side of a cube is increased by 100%, then by what percentage is the surface area of the cube increased?
questions.questionHtml: If the side of a cube is increased by 100%, then by what percentage is the surface area of the cube increased?
questions.solution:
Let edge of a smaller cube be 1 m. Then, edge of larger cube be 2 m.

Surface area of smaller cube = 6 × (1)2 = 6 m2

And, surface area of larger cube = 6 × (2)2 = 24 m2

% increase in surface area = (\(\frac{24-6}{{6}}\) × 100) = 300%

questions.question: Three cubes of sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 1 cm are melted to form a new cube. The surface area of the new cube is:‐
questions.questionHtml: Three cubes of sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 1 cm are melted to form a new cube. The surface area of the new cube is:‐
questions.solution:
Surface area of cube = 6 × a2, where a is side of the cube

Volume of cube = a3

Volume of cube with side 1 cm = 13 = 1 cm3

Volume of cube with side 6 cm = 63 = 216 cm³

Volume of cube with side 8 cm = 83 = 512 cm³

Total Volume = 1 + 216 + 512 = 729 cm³

Side of new cube = a cm

Volume of new cube = a³ cm³

a³ = 729

⇒ a = 9

Side of cube = 9 cm

Surface Area = 6 × a² = 6 × 9² = 486 cm²

∴ Surface area of the new formed cube 486 cm2

questions.question: A wall of dimensions 50 m × 30 m × 40 m is to be built with bricks of length 3 m, breadth 2 m, and height 1 m. The contractor has ordered 6500 bricks. How many more bricks would be required?
questions.questionHtml: A wall of dimensions 50 m × 30 m × 40 m is to be built with bricks of length 3 m, breadth 2 m, and height 1 m. The contractor has ordered 6500 bricks. How many more bricks would be required?
questions.solution:
Volume of Wall = 50 × 30 × 40 = 60000 m3, Volume of Brick = 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 m3.

 

Total Bricks = 60000 ÷ 6 = 10000, Additional Bricks = 10000 - 6500 = 3500.

questions.question: A cuboidal tank has 25000 litres of water. If the depth of the cuboid is 1/5 of its length and breadth is 1/8 of its length, then the length of the tank is:
questions.questionHtml: A cuboidal tank has 25000 litres of water. If the depth of the cuboid is 1/5 of its length and breadth is 1/8 of its length, then the length of the tank is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Volume of tank = 25000 litres

Depth of cuboid = 1/5 of length

Breadth of cuboid = 1/8 of length

Formula∶ 

Volume of a cuboid = lbh

Calculation:

As we know,

1000 litres = 1 m3

25000 litres = 25 m3

Let the length of the tank be x m.

Depth of tank = x × 1/5 = x/5

Breadth of tank = x × 1/8 = x/8

Formula∶ Volume of a cuboid = lbh

x × x/5 × x/8 = 25

⇒ x3 = 53 × 23

⇒ x = 5 × 2 = 10 m

∴ The correct answer is 10 m.

questions.question: The floor of an office has dimensions 5 m × 3 m. The cost of painting the walls is ₹8,640 at the rate of 60/m 2 . Find the height of the room (in m).
questions.questionHtml: The floor of an office has dimensions 5 m × 3 m. The cost of painting the walls is ₹8,640 at the rate of 60/m<sup>2</sup>. Find the height of the room (in m).
questions.solution:
Area = Cost of painting / Rate of painting ⇒ 8640 / 60 = 144 m2

Area of four walls = 2 × (l + b) × h ⇒ 144 = 2 × (5 + 3) × h ⇒ 144 = 16 × h

h = 144 / 16 ⇒ 9 m

questions.question: The ratio of the length, width and height of a cuboid is 60 ∶ 24 ∶ 7 and the length of each of its four space diagonals is 130 cm. What is the volume ( in cm 3 ) of the cuboid?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the length, width and height of a cuboid is 60 ∶ 24 ∶ 7 and the length of each of its four space diagonals is 130 cm. What is the volume (in cm3) of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
d2 = l2 + b2 + h2 ⇒ 1302 = (60x)2 + (24x)2 + (7x)2 ⇒ x = 2

length = 60 × 2 = 120 cm, width = 24 × 2 = 48 cm, height = 7 × 2 = 14 cm

questions.question: If the diagonal of a cube is √27 cm. Then what is its total surface area?
questions.questionHtml: If the diagonal of a cube is √27 cm. Then what is its total surface area?
questions.solution:
Diagonal of a cube = √3 × a

As, diagonal of cube = √27 cm = √3 × a ⇒ a = 3 cm

Total surface area of Cube = 6 × side2 = 6 × 32 = 6 × 9 = 54 cm2

questions.question: A box has a length of 10 m, a width of 6 m and a height of 4 m. How many cubes of volume 15 m 3 can be accommodated in the box?
questions.questionHtml: A box has a length of 10 m, a width of 6 m and a height of 4 m. How many cubes of volume 15 m<sup>3</sup> can be accommodated in the box?
questions.solution:
Given:

Length = 10 m; Width = 6 m; Height = 4 m and Volume of the small cube = 15 m3

Concept:

  • Volume of a cuboid = Length × Width × Height

  • Volume of a cube = (side)3

Calculation:

Volume of the box = 10 × 6 × 4 = 240 m3

Volume of the small cube = 15 m3

∴ Number of the small cubes that can be accommodated in the box = 240/15 = 16

Hence, there are 16 cubes that can be accommodated in the box.
